title: Establish encoder correctness before generalizing model support
description: Live Anima audit: plain conditioning matches core bitwise but the node drops attention_mask, t5xxl_ids and t5xxl_weights; emphasis loses its intended metadata channel; BREAK crashes on ragged batches. Define independent encoder-stream contracts, preserve required metadata, and verify static and scheduled paths before generalization. Correct the research harness assertion that assumes Qwen and T5 sequence lengths must match. Keep inherited Qwen emphasis-fragment tokenization separate from node-specific bugs.

title: Fix headless API imports and autocomplete ownership races
description: First batch from the usage-findings audit: allow API modules to import without aiohttp/server or a live PromptServer.instance; preserve live route registration. Prevent stale autocomplete responses, errors, blur timers, and other nodes from overwriting or hiding the focused popup. Add focused Python and JavaScript regression coverage and run review-mcp. Preserve the existing default-tag-file change and untracked research/data.
notes: Implemented headless API guards and autocomplete popup ownership/invalidation, preserving active error feedback and insertion. Validation: all 74 Python tests pass in installed ComfyUI Windows venv; 8 Node VM lifecycle tests pass. Baseline HEAD fails 4/5 new import checks and 7/8 lifecycle checks. review-mcp attempted against HEAD; provider returned HTTP 429 (5-hour usage limit), artifacts /tmp/review-mcp-run-40e6nr23. Browser smoke check in progress.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: 74 Python tests, 8 frontend lifecycle checks, and real Chromium fixture checks for stale cross-node responses, click insertion, keyboard insertion and Escape dismissal. title: Reconcile remaining autocomplete ranking and token-counter findings
description: Audit follow-up: frequency reranking only sees the backend top 20, so frequently used omitted tags cannot be promoted. Counter still uses a fixed CLIP tokenizer and 75-token chunks; a single 80-token word produces [80] without a chunk boundary. Existing wildcard estimates, metadata, and leaf-completion fixes pass tests. Verify remaining boundary-marker behavior and perceived latency in a live browser before claiming those resolved.
